title: The Sunless Sea
subtitle: Beneath Black Waters, Ancient Dreams Stir

setting.name: The Darklake and Its Shores
setting.description: The Sunless Sea — known locally as the Darklake — is a vast underground ocean stretching beyond the reach of any light source, its black waters lit from below by phosphorescent creatures and volcanic thermal vents. Rocky islands dot the surface, some large enough to hold settlements, others barely breaking the waterline. The air is warm and humid, carrying the smell of brine and sulfur. Kuo-toa communities cling to the islands and shorelines, worshipping whatever entity captures their collective imagination — and currently, the aboleth Ssylurex has captured it utterly, feeding the kuo-toa visions of a false god it calls the Deep Father.
setting.atmosphere: An atmosphere of vast, unknowable space — the darkness above the water is absolute, the water itself is deep beyond sounding, and the sense of being watched from below is constant and pervasive. The Sunless Sea is beautiful in its terrible way: bioluminescent creatures create patterns of light beneath the surface, thermal vents produce columns of warmth in the cold air, and the sound of water lapping against stone echoes endlessly. But something intelligent moves beneath those waters, and its dreams seep into the minds of everyone nearby.

keyLocations.name: The Darklake Shore
keyLocations.description: The tunnel network from scenario 2 eventually opens onto the shore of the Darklake — a rocky beach of smooth black stone littered with the remnants of fishing boats and abandoned camps. The water stretches into darkness in every direction, and the shore curves away into the gloom. A crude dock juts into the water, and nearby, the glow of cooking fires marks a small kuo-toa fishing camp.
features: Rocky beach with abandoned boats (some repairable with DC 14 Carpenter's Tools or Athletics)
Crude dock with 2 fishing boats that can be taken or traded for
Kuo-toa fishing camp with 8-10 non-hostile fisher-folk
Tidal pools containing unusual Underdark marine life — blind cave fish, luminescent jellyfish, and tiny crustaceans
encounters: Roleplaying with kuo-toa fishers who are friendly but strange — their speech is fragmented and they keep glancing at the water as if listening to something beneath
A DC 13 Wisdom save as the aboleth's dream-influence washes over newcomers to the shore, sending vivid images of a vast, benevolent presence beneath the waves
secrets: The kuo-toa fishers are all under the aboleth's subtle influence — they genuinely believe the Deep Father is a benevolent deity and will become hostile if challenged on this
One of the fishers, Ploopploopeen, is the deposed arch-priest who has been resisting the aboleth's influence. He can be identified by the chain-marks on his wrists where he was bound before escaping

keyLocations.name: Sloobludop — The Kuo-toa City
keyLocations.description: A ramshackle city of coral, bone, and scavenged materials built on and around a large island in the Darklake. Towers of lashed-together zurkhwood lean at precarious angles, bridges of woven kelp span the gaps between structures, and the entire settlement radiates a feverish, fanatical energy. The kuo-toa are preparing for a great ceremony — the Offering to the Deep Father — and the streets are filled with chanting, dancing, and the construction of a massive altar at the island's highest point.
features: A city of 200+ kuo-toa, most of whom are fervent worshippers of the Deep Father
The Great Altar — a platform of coral and bone being constructed at the island's peak for the Offering ceremony
An underwater temple entrance visible at low tide — the path to the aboleth's lair
Markets selling bizarre Underdark goods: glowing fungi, cave fish, zurkhwood items, and 'sacred water' blessed by the Deep Father
The old temple of Blibdoolpoolp (the kuo-toa's traditional goddess), now abandoned and defaced
encounters: The current arch-priest, Bloppblippodd, who is utterly devoted to the Deep Father and plans to sacrifice prisoners at the Offering ceremony
Kuo-toa whips (enforcers) who patrol the streets ensuring compliance with the new religious order
A market encounter where strange Underdark items can be traded for
secrets: The Offering ceremony is actually a mass psychic ritual that will dramatically amplify the aboleth's influence, extending its reach throughout the Darklake region and into the surrounding tunnel systems

The kuo-toa's collective belief is so strong that it is actually creating a minor divine spark — if the ceremony is completed, the 'Deep Father' entity they are creating will become partially real, a newborn god-fragment under the aboleth's control

keyLocations.name: The Sea Caves
keyLocations.description: A network of partially submerged caves along the far shore of the island, accessible at low tide or by swimming. The caves are sacred to the old faith of Blibdoolpoolp and have been sealed by the new priesthood. Within, ancient kuo-toa murals tell the history of the Darklake settlement, and a hidden passage leads to the aboleth's underwater temple.
features: Partially submerged tunnels requiring swimming through 20-30 ft sections (DC 12 Athletics to swim without difficulty)
Ancient kuo-toa murals depicting the aboleth's first appearance and the gradual subversion of their faith
A breathable air pocket with a shrine to Blibdoolpoolp, still maintained by Ploopploopeen
A hidden passage (DC 15 Perception to find) leading down through underwater tunnels to the aboleth's temple
encounters: 2 chuuls that guard the approach to the aboleth's territory
Environmental hazards: rising water levels, strong currents (DC 13 Athletics or be swept into deeper water), slippery stone surfaces
secrets: The murals in the sea caves tell a complete history — the aboleth arrived centuries ago and has been slowly shaping the kuo-toa over generations, waiting for the right moment to execute its plan
The shrine to Blibdoolpoolp contains a sacred weapon — the Trident of the Old Faith — that grants advantage on saving throws against the aboleth's psychic abilities when wielded

keyLocations.name: The Aboleth's Temple
keyLocations.description: Deep beneath the Darklake, in a cavern filled with water except for a raised stone platform at its center, dwells Ssylurex the aboleth. The temple was ancient before the kuo-toa arrived — its walls are covered in carvings from a civilization that predates the current age, depicting the aboleths' dominion over the primordial world. Ssylurex floats in the dark water, its massive body trailing tentacles, three alien eyes regarding everything with cold, patient intelligence. It has been alive for millennia and considers all surface races — including the mind flayers — to be young, foolish, and manipulable.
features: Submerged temple chamber (100 ft by 80 ft, water depth 20 ft, central platform 20 ft by 20 ft and 5 ft above water)
Ancient carvings predating all current civilizations
A psychic amplification device of aboleth construction on the platform — the mechanism that will power the Offering ceremony
Treasure accumulated over centuries scattered on the lake floor around the platform
encounters: Ssylurex the aboleth (CR 10) — a terrifyingly intelligent and ancient creature with powerful psychic abilities
2 chuuls serving as the aboleth's bodyguards
The temple itself — rising water, illusory terrain, and psychic interference make the environment hostile
secrets: Ssylurex has been in contact with the elder brain — they are ancient rivals who have formed a temporary alliance of convenience. The aboleth provides the elder brain with information about surface-world defenses in exchange for being left alone in its domain

The psychic amplification device on the platform can be reversed — instead of amplifying the aboleth's influence, it can be used to broadcast a psychic disruption that weakens the elder brain's reach (if the party discovers this, it becomes a crucial advantage in scenario 4)

synopsis: Fleeing the drow, the party reaches the shores of the Darklake — the Sunless Sea — and discovers a kuo-toa civilization in the grip of a false religion. The aboleth Ssylurex has been manipulating the kuo-toa for centuries, slowly building toward a grand ceremony that will amplify its psychic power to godlike levels. With the help of a deposed kuo-toa priest, the party must navigate the alien culture of Sloobludop, explore the sea caves to find the path to the aboleth's underwater temple, and confront the ancient creature before its plan reaches fruition. Along the way, they discover that the aboleth is connected to the elder brain — ancient rivals turned temporary allies — and find a potential weapon against the mind flayer threat.
hook: The party emerges from the tunnel network onto the shores of an underground sea that stretches into impossible darkness. The first thing they encounter is a kuo-toa fishing camp, its inhabitants friendly but unsettling — they speak of the 'Deep Father' with glazed-eyed reverence and keep urging the party to attend the upcoming Offering ceremony at Sloobludop. Something is very wrong here. Then a figure emerges from the shadows — a kuo-toa with chain-marks on his wrists and desperation in his bulging eyes. 'The Deep Father is no god,' he whispers. 'It is a monster. And it is about to devour my people's minds.'

acts.title: Act 1: Shores of the Sunless Sea
acts.description: The party arrives at the Darklake, encounters the kuo-toa, and learns about the Deep Father religion. They meet Ploopploopeen, the deposed arch-priest, who reveals the truth about the aboleth's manipulation.
objectives: Make contact with the kuo-toa fishers
Learn about the Deep Father and the upcoming Offering ceremony
Meet Ploopploopeen and learn the truth about the aboleth

scenes.name: The Black Water
scenes.description: The party reaches the Darklake shore and experiences the vast, alien majesty of the underground sea. They encounter the kuo-toa fishing camp and have their first brush with the aboleth's psychic influence.
scenes.readAloud: "The tunnel opens and the darkness before you is not the darkness of stone but the darkness of open water. You stand on a shore of smooth black rock, and before you stretches a sea without a horizon — the Darklake, the Sunless Sea. The water is black and still as obsidian, its surface broken only by the faintest concentric ripples and, far out, the ghostly glow of phosphorescent creatures drifting in the depths like underwater stars. The air is warm, humid, and carries the smell of brine and sulfur. To your left, crude fishing boats are drawn up on the shore, and beyond them, the glow of small cooking fires marks a camp. Squat, fish-like figures move around the fires — kuo-toa, their goggle eyes reflecting the firelight, their scaled skin glistening with moisture. As you watch, a wave of something washes over you — not water but thought. A vision of vast, benevolent presence beneath the waves. Safety. Worship. Home."

skillChecks.success: You recognize the vision as external influence — something is projecting these feelings of safety and worship into your mind. The sensation passes, but you know it will return.
skillChecks.failure: The vision of the Deep Father feels genuine and comforting. You must succeed on a DC 14 Insight check to recognize that the feeling is not your own.

skillChecks.success: Among the kuo-toa fishers, you notice one who hangs back from the others — thin, scarred, with chain-marks on his wrists. He watches the party with desperate intensity rather than the glazed devotion of the others.
skillChecks.failure: The kuo-toa all seem the same to you — strange, fish-like beings engaged in their daily routines.

skillChecks.success: You identify the kuo-toa as amphibious humanoids known for their fervent religiosity and their unique ability to create minor deities through collective belief. If enough kuo-toa believe in a god, it can actually become partially real.
skillChecks.failure: The kuo-toa are clearly aquatic humanoids, but you know little about their culture or abilities.

scenes.roleplayNotes: The Darklake should inspire awe and unease in equal measure. Describe the vast, empty darkness, the impossibility of seeing the far shore, the strange lights beneath the water. The kuo-toa fishers are friendly but alien — they do not blink, they speak in gurgling voices, and they keep trying to convert the party to the Deep Father faith. Ploopploopeen's desperation should be palpable — he has been fighting the aboleth's influence alone and is running out of time before the Offering ceremony.
loot: Trade goods from the fishing camp: salted cave fish (10 days rations), a net of luminescent jellyfish (light source, worth 5 gp), crude fishing equipment
Ploopploopeen offers a pearl necklace (worth 50 gp) if the party agrees to help

scenes.name: The Holy City
scenes.description: The party travels by boat to Sloobludop and sees the kuo-toa city in the grip of religious fervor. The Great Altar is being constructed, the ceremony approaches, and the party must navigate a fanatical population.
scenes.readAloud: "Sloobludop rises from the Darklake like a fever dream. Buildings of coral, bone, and scavenged wood lean against each other at impossible angles, connected by bridges of braided kelp that sway with every step. Kuo-toa are everywhere — hundreds of them, chanting, dancing, working with frenzied energy on a massive structure at the island's peak. The Great Altar. It is a platform of white coral and bleached bone, rising three stories above the highest rooftop, its surface carved with symbols that make your eyes water to look at. The air hums with psychic energy — you can feel the collective belief of the entire city pressing against your mind, a choir of whispered worship directed at something beneath the water. And sometimes, when the chanting peaks, you swear you can see it — a vast shadow moving far below the surface, too large to be real, too deliberate to be a trick of the light."

skillChecks.success: You convincingly pose as pilgrims or traders, gaining access to the city without arousing suspicion from the kuo-toa whips.
skillChecks.failure: The kuo-toa whips are suspicious and assign an escort to watch the party — a minder who reports their movements to Arch-priest Bloppblippodd.

skillChecks.success: You recognize the altar construction as a genuine divine ritual framework — the kuo-toa are building something that could actually create a god-fragment if enough belief is channeled through it. This is more dangerous than a simple con.
skillChecks.failure: The altar appears to be a normal (if bizarre) religious construction.

skillChecks.success: The arch-priest Bloppblippodd is not merely a fanatic — she has been directly enslaved by the aboleth through its Enslave ability. Her devotion is not faith but psychic compulsion.
skillChecks.failure: Bloppblippodd seems genuinely and terrifyingly devoted to the Deep Father.

scenes.roleplayNotes: Sloobludop should feel like visiting a cult compound at its most fervent. The kuo-toa are not evil — they are a people desperate for meaning and protection in a hostile world, and the aboleth has exploited that desperation. The Offering ceremony is their apocalypse and their rapture rolled into one. Make the players feel the weight of the collective delusion and the genuine danger of trying to disrupt it. If the party is discovered as unbelievers, the entire city could turn against them.
loot: Market goods: Darklake pearls (5 gp each, 3 available), a zurkhwood buckler (shield), cave fish oil (burns as lamp oil), strange coral carvings (worth 2-5 gp each)

acts.title: Act 2: Beneath the Waves
acts.description: The party explores the sea caves, finds the old shrine, recovers the Trident of the Old Faith, and discovers the underwater passage to the aboleth's temple. Environmental hazards and guardian creatures test their resolve.
objectives: Enter the sea caves and navigate the submerged passages
Discover the ancient kuo-toa murals and learn the aboleth's history
Find and claim the Trident of the Old Faith
Locate the underwater passage to the aboleth's temple

scenes.name: The Drowned Halls
scenes.description: The party enters the sea caves — partially submerged tunnels sacred to the old kuo-toa faith — and navigates water hazards while discovering the true history of the aboleth's presence.
scenes.readAloud: "Ploopploopeen leads you to a section of shoreline away from the main city, where weathered stone steps descend into black water. 'The old temple,' he says, his voice trembling. 'Bloppblippodd sealed it, but I know another way.' He dives beneath the surface and you follow, the cold water closing over your heads. The passage is short — twenty feet of swimming through darkness before you surface in a cave lit by natural phosphorescence. The walls are covered in murals painted in pigments that still glow after centuries: images of the kuo-toa building their first city, worshipping Blibdoolpoolp the Sea Mother, and then — a new figure in the paintings. Something vast, with three eyes and trailing tentacles, rising from the depths. The kuo-toa in the murals bow. They change. Their eyes become vacant, their mouths open in perpetual song. The history of a people being consumed, painted on the walls of their forgotten temple."

skillChecks.success: You swim through the submerged sections of the sea caves without difficulty, reaching the air pockets and dry chambers efficiently.
skillChecks.failure: The strong currents in the submerged passages pull you off course. You take 1d4 bludgeoning damage from being thrown against the cave walls and surface gasping.

skillChecks.success: The murals tell a complete story spanning centuries. The aboleth arrived during a time of kuo-toa vulnerability, posing as a protector. Each generation fell deeper under its influence. The current ceremony is the final step in a plan that has been centuries in the making.
skillChecks.failure: The murals are clearly historical but the full narrative is difficult to piece together from the alien artistic style.

skillChecks.success: You find a hidden alcove in the shrine chamber containing the Trident of the Old Faith — a coral-and-pearl weapon that radiates faint protective magic.
skillChecks.failure: The shrine chamber appears to be empty of anything useful beyond the murals.

combatEncounters.tactics: The chuuls lurk in the submerged sections of the caves, attacking anyone who enters the water. They use their claws to grapple targets and drag them underwater, then use their tentacles to paralyze grappled creatures. They are fiercely territorial but will retreat if both are reduced below half HP, fleeing toward the aboleth's temple.
combatEncounters.terrain: Sea cave chamber (40 ft by 30 ft). Half the floor is submerged in 5-ft-deep water. The water section counts as difficult terrain for non-aquatic creatures. Stalactites provide half cover for ranged attacks. The submerged passage to the aboleth's temple is visible at the far end of the chamber.

scenes.roleplayNotes: The sea caves are a place of lost history and quiet tragedy. The murals should tell the aboleth's story through images rather than words — make the players piece together the narrative from visual descriptions. Ploopploopeen's reactions add emotional weight: he weeps when he sees the murals depicting his ancestors' freedom, and his resolve hardens when he sees the progression of their enslavement. The Trident of the Old Faith is both a practical weapon and a symbol — it represents the possibility of freeing the kuo-toa from the aboleth's grip.
loot: Trident of the Old Faith (uncommon, +1 trident, while attuned: advantage on saving throws against being charmed or having thoughts read; bearer can cast protection from evil and good once per long rest)
Ancient kuo-toa offerings at the shrine: 6 black pearls (10 gp each), a coral circlet (25 gp), and a sealed jar of blessed water (functions as 3 vials of holy water)

scenes.name: The Deep Father's Dream
scenes.description: As the party prepares to descend to the aboleth's temple, they experience the full force of its psychic influence — a shared vision/dream sequence that reveals the aboleth's nature and its connection to the elder brain.
scenes.readAloud: "As you rest in the air pocket of the sea caves, preparing for the descent, the water around you begins to glow with a deep, hypnotic blue. The glow intensifies until it fills your vision, and then you are no longer in the cave. You float in an endless ocean, warm and dark, and something vast moves below you — a shadow so large it has its own horizon. Three eyes open in the darkness, each the size of a house, each older than civilization. A voice fills your mind, not in words but in absolute knowledge, as if you have always known what it says: 'I remember when your kind crawled from the mud. I remember when the stars had different names. I will be here when your gods are forgotten and your cities are dust. The children above pray to me because I am what was, what is, and what will be. You cannot fight time.' And then, deeper still, beyond the aboleth, you sense something else — a web of thought spreading through the Underdark like roots through soil. An intelligence that makes even this ancient creature seem small. The elder brain. The aboleth turns one vast eye toward it, and in that gaze you read something unexpected: fear."

skillChecks.success: You resist the full weight of the vision, recognizing it as the aboleth's psychic projection. You see through the grandeur to the creature's actual limitations — it is powerful but not all-knowing, ancient but not invincible. You also clearly perceive the aboleth's fear of the elder brain.
skillChecks.failure: The vision overwhelms you. You are frightened of the aboleth for 1 hour (disadvantage on ability checks and attack rolls while you can see the aboleth). This condition can be ended by a calm emotions spell or a DC 14 Charisma check as an action.

skillChecks.success: Within the vision, you perceive the psychic connection between the aboleth and the elder brain — and recognize that it is a two-way link. The psychic amplification device in the aboleth's temple could theoretically be reversed to disrupt the elder brain's network.
skillChecks.failure: The connection between the aboleth and something deeper is apparent but its nature and potential vulnerability are unclear.

scenes.roleplayNotes: This is a pivotal narrative moment — the first time the party directly experiences the elder brain's presence, even indirectly. The vision should be genuinely awe-inspiring and terrifying. The aboleth's age and power are real, but so is its fear of the elder brain. This reveals the campaign's power hierarchy: the aboleth is dangerous, but it is merely a player in the elder brain's larger game. The vision also provides crucial strategic information if the party succeeds on their saves — the psychic amplifier can be turned against the elder brain, setting up a key advantage for scenario 4.

acts.title: Act 3: The Deep Father Falls
acts.description: The party descends to the aboleth's underwater temple, confronts Ssylurex, and must stop the Offering ceremony before it creates a god-fragment under the aboleth's control. The climactic battle takes place in and around the submerged temple, with the ceremony happening above on the surface.
objectives: Confront and defeat or drive off Ssylurex
Destroy or reverse the psychic amplification device
Stop the Offering ceremony in Sloobludop
Free the kuo-toa from the aboleth's influence

scenes.name: Into the Temple
scenes.description: The party descends through the underwater passage to the aboleth's ancient temple and confronts Ssylurex in its domain.
scenes.readAloud: "The underwater passage descends steeply, the water growing warmer as you swim deeper. The walls are carved with symbols that predate every civilization you know — angular, alien, and radiating a faint psychic hum. After what feels like an eternity, the passage opens into a vast underwater chamber, and your heads break the surface beside a raised stone platform at its center. The temple. Columns of black stone rise from the water, carved with writhing tentacle motifs. The ceiling is lost in darkness above. On the platform sits a device of unknown construction — a crystalline sphere nested in tentacle-shaped brackets of dark metal, pulsing with blue-white light in rhythm with the faint chanting you can feel more than hear from the city above. And there, in the water, circling the platform with glacial patience, is the aboleth. Ssylurex. Twenty feet long, its body is a mass of grey-green flesh trailing tentacles, three alien eyes arranged vertically along its head, each one fixing on you with an intelligence that has had millennia to sharpen. It does not attack immediately. It regards you with something like curiosity — or amusement."

skillChecks.success: You understand the psychic amplification device and how to reverse its polarity. Doing so requires 2 rounds of uninterrupted work at the device (Arcana DC 13 each round). Once reversed, it will broadcast a psychic disruption that breaks the aboleth's hold on the kuo-toa and weakens psychic creatures within a 1-mile radius.
skillChecks.failure: The device is clearly important to the aboleth's plan but its mechanisms are beyond your understanding.

skillChecks.success: The chanting from above is reaching a crescendo — the Offering ceremony is beginning. If it completes (approximately 10 rounds), the collective belief of the kuo-toa will create a god-fragment bound to the aboleth's will.
skillChecks.failure: You can hear chanting but cannot gauge how close the ceremony is to completion.

skillChecks.success: The aboleth is not attacking immediately because it is curious and arrogant — it has not been challenged in centuries and wants to understand its opponents before destroying them. This gives the party a brief window to negotiate, distract, or prepare.

combatEncounters.tactics: Ssylurex fights from the water, using its tentacles to attack anyone on the platform and its Enslave ability (DC 14 Wisdom save) to turn party members against each other. It uses its lair actions: at initiative count 20, it can create illusory images throughout the temple, conjure a pool of slime under one creature, or psychically command all enslaved creatures to attack. The chuuls emerge from the water on opposite sides of the platform, trying to drag characters into the deep water where the aboleth has advantage. If the party begins reversing the psychic amplifier, Ssylurex prioritizes stopping them. The Trident of the Old Faith grants advantage on saves against its psychic abilities. If reduced to 40 HP or below, Ssylurex attempts to flee into the depths — it has survived millennia by knowing when to retreat.
combatEncounters.terrain: Submerged temple (100 ft by 80 ft, water depth 20 ft). Central stone platform (20 ft by 20 ft, 5 ft above water level). Four columns provide half cover. The water is difficult terrain for non-aquatic creatures. Creatures in the water are subject to the aboleth's tentacle attacks (10-ft reach from water surface). The psychic amplifier is on the platform.

scenes.roleplayNotes: This is the scenario's climactic confrontation. The aboleth should feel genuinely alien and terrifying — not evil in a human sense but utterly without empathy, viewing all other creatures as tools or food. Its dialogue (transmitted psychically) should be ancient and contemptuous: 'I was old when the elves were young. What are you to challenge me?' The dual objective — fight the aboleth AND stop the ceremony — creates dynamic tension. If the party splits up to send someone to disrupt the ceremony above while others fight below, reward that tactical thinking. The ticking clock of the ceremony adds urgency to every round of combat.
loot: Aboleth's hoard (scattered on the temple floor): 350 gp in ancient coins, a driftglobe (common magic item), a cloak of the manta ray (uncommon, allows breathing underwater and 60-ft swim speed), 3 black sapphires (50 gp each)

If the psychic amplifier is reversed rather than destroyed: Psychic Disruptor Fragment (quest item — provides crucial advantage against the elder brain in scenario 4, grants one-time use of a psychic disruption field that gives all allies within 30 ft advantage on saves against psychic effects for 10 minutes)

scenes.name: Dawn Beneath the Waves
scenes.description: With the aboleth defeated or driven off and the ceremony disrupted, the kuo-toa awaken from their collective delusion. Ploopploopeen works to restore order, and the party learns what lies ahead — the path to the elder brain's domain.
scenes.readAloud: "The psychic amplifier pulses once, brilliantly, then goes dark — or rather, it reverses, sending a wave of clarity rippling outward through the water, through the stone, up through the island and into the minds of every kuo-toa in Sloobludop. The chanting above falters. Stops. Is replaced by confusion, then wailing, as hundreds of minds suddenly freed from centuries of psychic manipulation try to process what has been done to them. In the temple, the water stills. Ssylurex is gone — fled into the deepest reaches of the Darklake, wounded and furious but alive. Ploopploopeen stands on the temple platform, the Trident of the Old Faith in his hands (if given), and sends out a pulse of rapport through the water — his own voice, reaching his people for the first time in years. The message is simple: 'We are free. We were deceived. But we are free.' When you surface in Sloobludop, the city is in chaos — but it is the chaos of awakening, not destruction. Kuo-toa weep, embrace, tear down the Great Altar stone by stone. And through the tumult, you feel it again — that vast psychic presence from the deep, the elder brain, and it is closer now. It knows you are coming."

skillChecks.success: You help Ploopploopeen restore order, and the grateful kuo-toa provide the party with boats, supplies, and detailed knowledge of the waterways leading to the far shore of the Darklake — the approach to the mind flayer territories.
skillChecks.failure: The chaos takes longer to settle and the party must wait before the kuo-toa can help them.

skillChecks.success: You sense the elder brain's awareness focused on you like a searchlight. It has been observing through the aboleth's psychic network all along. It knows your faces, your names, and your capabilities. The advantage of surprise is gone — but you have the psychic disruptor.
skillChecks.failure: The psychic presence is noticed but its full implications are not clear.

scenes.roleplayNotes: This is a moment of triumph tempered by the knowledge that the greatest challenge lies ahead. The kuo-toa's awakening should be emotional — these are people who have been enslaved for centuries, and their liberation is a genuine good that the party has accomplished. But the elder brain's awareness should cast a shadow over the victory. Ploopploopeen's gratitude is boundless, and he provides the party with everything they need for the final leg of their journey. The stage is set for scenario 4.
loot: Kuo-toa gratitude gifts: 2 potions of water breathing, a net of holding (functions as a net but is magical and cannot be cut by nonmagical means), 100 gp in Darklake pearls and coral
Ploopploopeen's blessing: advantage on the first saving throw against any mind flayer psychic ability (one-time blessing, narratively described as a shield of liberated collective will)
Darklake navigation charts: detailed maps of the waterways connecting the Sunless Sea to the tunnels leading to the mind flayer territories

npcsInvolved.name: Ploopploopeen
npcsInvolved.description: The deposed arch-priest of Blibdoolpoolp, the kuo-toa's traditional goddess. Thin and scarred from his imprisonment, with chain-marks on his wrists, but his bulging eyes burn with desperate determination. He speaks in short, urgent sentences, always glancing over his shoulder.
npcsInvolved.motivation: Ploopploopeen wants to free his people from the aboleth's influence and restore the worship of Blibdoolpoolp. He is willing to risk everything — including his life — to stop the Offering ceremony. He genuinely cares about his people and views the party as his last hope.

npcsInvolved.name: Bloppblippodd
npcsInvolved.description: The current arch-priest of the Deep Father faith, a large and powerful kuo-toa who has been directly enslaved by the aboleth through its Enslave ability. Her eyes have a glazed, vacant quality even as she speaks with fervent conviction about the Deep Father's glory. She is a victim, not a villain, but she is dangerous.
npcsInvolved.motivation: Under the aboleth's control, Bloppblippodd believes absolutely in the Deep Father and will kill to protect the faith and the ceremony. If freed from the aboleth's influence, she will be horrified by what she has done and become a valuable ally.

npcsInvolved.name: Ssylurex the Aboleth
npcsInvolved.description: An ancient aboleth that has dwelt beneath the Darklake for millennia, patiently manipulating the kuo-toa over generations. Twenty feet long, with grey-green flesh trailing tentacles and three vertical eyes of cold, alien intelligence. It does not hate — it is simply too ancient and too alien to conceive of other beings as anything but tools.
npcsInvolved.motivation: Ssylurex wants to amplify its psychic power through the kuo-toa's collective belief, creating a god-fragment under its control. This is the culmination of a centuries-long plan. It also maintains a relationship with the elder brain — ancient rivals who have formed an alliance of convenience, each believing they are using the other.

rewards.gold: 500 gp total (aboleth's hoard, kuo-toa gifts, market finds)
items: Trident of the Old Faith (uncommon, +1, advantage vs. charm/mind-reading, protection from evil and good 1/long rest)
Cloak of the Manta Ray (uncommon, water breathing, 60-ft swim speed)
Psychic Disruptor Fragment (quest item — advantage against elder brain in scenario 4)
rewards.story: The party has freed an entire civilization from centuries of psychic slavery, confronted an ancient aboleth, and discovered the connection between the aboleth and the elder brain. The psychic disruptor provides a potential tactical advantage for the final confrontation. The aboleth escaped but is wounded and diminished. The kuo-toa owe the party a debt of gratitude. The path to the mind flayer colony is clear, and the elder brain knows they are coming.

twists: The kuo-toa's collective belief is so powerful that the Offering ceremony would actually create a minor god-fragment — a real divine entity under the aboleth's control. The stakes are higher than simply stopping a ritual.

The aboleth and the elder brain are ancient rivals turned temporary allies — each believes they are manipulating the other. The aboleth fears the elder brain and has been providing intelligence in exchange for being left alone.

The psychic amplification device in the aboleth's temple can be reversed to create a disruption field that weakens the elder brain — a crucial advantage for scenario 4 that rewards thorough exploration.

The aboleth is not truly defeated — it flees into the depths when wounded, and its centuries-long patience means it will eventually return. The party has won the battle but the aboleth will outlast them all.
dmTips: The kuo-toa culture should be played as genuinely alien, not just 'fish people.' Their language is gurgling and wet, their body language involves flaring fins and changing skin patterns, and their concept of divinity is fundamentally different from surface religions. Make the players work to understand them.

The aboleth encounter should feel like confronting something truly ancient and powerful. Ssylurex has survived millennia — it is not going to make stupid mistakes. Play it as the most intelligent opponent the party has faced: it evaluates, adapts, and retreats when necessary. Its psychic dialogue should be condescending and alien.

The Offering ceremony ticking clock creates dynamic tension. Give the party regular updates on how close the ceremony is to completion — 'The chanting above grows louder, more rhythmic. You can feel the psychic pressure building.' This forces them to balance thoroughness with urgency.

If the drow pursuit from scenario 2 is still active, Commander Ilvara may arrive at the Darklake during this scenario, creating a three-way conflict between the party, the drow, and the aboleth. Use this complication if the party needs additional challenge.

The psychic disruptor fragment from the reversed amplifier is a crucial scenario 4 advantage. Make sure the party has the opportunity to discover it — if they destroy the device instead of reversing it, provide an alternative path (perhaps the trident can be modified, or Ploopploopeen's blessing provides a weaker version of the same effect).
